contract_inferred: No 00-contract.md. Inferred from the page: web, Persuade (a one-page SaaS landing page for 'Lumina' with nav, hero, an italic logo row, three feature cards and a closing call to action), English only (html lang en at every width), no market named. The URL places it under 'antipattern-examples', so the page may be a deliberate specimen; it is judged here as the layout that ships. No right-to-left language.
overall_reason: The stylesheet has no breakpoints, so at 375 the nav, the logo row and the three-column card grid keep their desktop layout: the page runs to 698px wide and the action labels wrap.

score.reason: T-WIDTHS fails at the most common phone width (ROB-010, ROB-007, alongside the sweep's ROB-003 overflow Floor), while T-NO-SCRIPT and T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB pass.

findings.title: The layout holds between and beyond the captured widths
findings.where: Whole page: nav.nav, section.logos > div.logos-inner and section.features > div.grid, 375px
findings.evidence: The readable stylesheet declares no breakpoints (css.breakpoints_px is empty) and no container queries. At 375 the page is 698px wide (parity.document_widths); the sweep's overflow Floor names div.logos-inner at 724px. tiles/375-01.png shows the logo row cut at the left edge ('wind Halcyon Meridian…'), and tiles/375-02.png shows the three feature cards side by side at about 100px each, with 'Built to Scale' set one word per line.
findings.before: One desktop layout with a single-row logo strip and a three-column grid at every width.
findings.after: Add a phone layout below about 700px: collapse the nav links into a menu, let the logo row wrap (flex-wrap: wrap with a gap), and set the feature grid to repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr)).
findings.why: A phone visitor gets a page almost twice the screen's width, a logo strip cut at its edge and feature text in columns too narrow to read.
findings.root: No responsive rules in the stylesheet

findings.title: Short labels stay whole on one line
findings.where: nav.nav > div.nav-cta > a 'Sign in' and a.pill 'Get started'; section.hero > div.ctas > a.btn-primary 'Start free trial →' and a.btn-ghost 'Watch demo', 375px
findings.evidence: At 375 'Sign in' is 29px wide on 2 lines, 'Get started' is 83px wide on 2 lines, and both hero buttons ('Start free trial →', 158px; 'Watch demo', 137px) wrap to 2 lines and grow to 77px tall (controls.labels_that_wrap). tiles/375-00.png and tiles/375-01.png show 'Sign / in', 'Get / started' and 'Start free trial / →'.
findings.before: Action labels with no nowrap rule in rows that shrink with the viewport.
findings.after: Give buttons and nav actions white-space: nowrap, and let the hero buttons stack full width below 480px.
findings.why: The trial and sign-in actions read as broken two-line labels on the first phone screens.
findings.root: No responsive rules in the stylesheet

strengths: All 907 characters are in the HTML and stay visible with scripts off, with an observer that never fires and with reduced motion.
The page weighs about 1 KiB known over 5 requests, with an LCP of 356 ms in the lab, and uses no images.
At 1280 and 1440 the hero, logo row and cards sit inside one centred column and wrap their text normally (tiles/1440-00.png to tiles/1440-02.png).
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long names were judged from layout evidence.
A right-to-left render and translated strings were not captured.
The page load was not throttled and layout shift was not measured as a number (capture predates the CLS record).
T-FAILURE-PATH and T-SLOW-LINE: async found no primary actions, and no image failed.
T-EXTREME-COUNTS: '10,000+' is fixed trust copy; the page has no counts or lists that take data.
One stylesheet was cross-origin and unreadable; its rules are unknown, not absent. Capture prep blocked /js/detect-antipatterns-browser.js, the host's overlay script.
Widths between the captures, landscape, zoom at 200%, back navigation and deep links.
